headline: Extremely rare Pokémon Red prototype cartridge surfaces at auction, starting at $25,000
summary: This "previously undocumented" Game Boy development cartridge, authenticated by PSA, features unique header data and is currently at a $25,000 bid.
details: A rare prototype copy of Pokémon Red for the Nintendo Game Boy, originally released in 1998, is currently up for auction. The current bid stands at $25,000 for this "incredibly rare" item.
The cartridge has been authenticated by PSA specialists, who confirmed 32KB of readable data. While a full data read wasn't possible, the accessible data is "technically unique."

PSA notes that the game data itself is "completely identical" to the U.S. release version. However, two changes were found in the ROM's header data, specifically at offset 0x014C and 0x014D, which do not affect gameplay.

This prototype uses a "previously undocumented" development board, though the part number DMG-(F)KGDB-01 has been seen before on other development cartridges. It features a sticker reading DMB-MBC-16M-FLASH.
The DMB likely refers to Dot Matrix Game (Game Boy's internal codename), and MBC indicates a Memory Bank Controller chip. The cartridge is also physically longer than a standard Game Boy cartridge.
Pokémon Red is a classic title that, along with Green and Blue, launched the global Pokémon franchise. Combined with Blue, it sold over 31 million copies.
The auction still has several days remaining, suggesting the final sale price could exceed the current $25,000 bid for this significant piece of gaming history.

headline: Remove image backgrounds in the browser with ONNX Runtime Web (no server)
summary: A new tool leverages ONNX Runtime Web and WebAssembly to perform image background removal directly in your browser. Your photos never leave your device, ensuring privacy and eliminating server costs.
details: A new tool, picfitter.online, allows users to remove image backgrounds directly in their browser without uploading photos to a server. This client-side processing is achieved using ONNX Runtime Web and WebAssembly.
The primary benefit is enhanced privacy, as images remain on the user's device. It also eliminates hosting costs associated with server-based background removal services.
The implementation involves running a segmentation model entirely in the browser. The model expects a 1024x1024 input, which is resized on a canvas and converted to a float tensor in NCHW order.

Careful normalization is crucial, as incorrect mean and standard deviation values can lead to poor masks. The raw output, a soft mask, is refined with a smoothstep curve on the alpha channel for cleaner outlines.
While effective for clear products on plain backgrounds, more complex images may still require manual touch-ups. The tool is free, requires no signup, and prioritizes user data privacy.
